stemMd: During inhalation at rest, contraction of the diaphragm has which immediate mechanical effect?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It produces oxygen chemically from carbon dioxide.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure in the lungs below atmospheric pressure.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It stops all movement of the rib cage.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It decreases thoracic volume and forces air out.

explanationMd: The diaphragm flattens as it contracts, enlarging the thoracic cavity. Expansion lowers alveolar pressure slightly below atmospheric pressure, causing air to flow inward. The driving cause is the pressure gradient produced by a volume change, not direct pumping of oxygen molecules.

distractorRationale.e: That describes a mechanism associated with expiration, not diaphragm contraction in inhalation.
distractorRationale.c: Air must have an open pathway into the lungs.
distractorRationale.a: Breathing moves gases; it does not perform this chemical conversion.
distractorRationale.d: The thorax can expand during inhalation.
